post.contentHtml:
A Year and a Half After Discover: Capital One by the Numbers

Capital One Financial (NYSE: COF) is a large U.S. credit card and consumer lending company. In its third-quarter 2026 results, announced on October 20, it gave investors figures that help gauge how far the Discover acquisition is showing up in cost savings and margin improvement. This article uses those results to lay out what the current share price says about the market's concerns.

Where the Stock Stands

  • As of intraday trading on November 2 (local time), the share price was around $211, up about 3% from the previous session's (October 30) close of $204.85. Data providers differ in timing, so please treat the figure as an approximate level.
  • The 52-week price range is roughly $174 to $260. The recent price sits in the lower half of that range.
  • Based on the data provided, the one-year price change is -7.52%, and the dividend is $3.2 per share (annual). The dividend yield works out to around 1.5% at the current price.
  • The average Wall Street analyst price target is about $255, and the average rating is "Buy" (this may vary by data aggregator).

Key Takeaways from Q3 Results

ItemQ3 2026
Net incomeAbout $3.5 billion ($5.61 diluted EPS)
Adjusted EPS$6.69 (excluding acquisition-related amortization and integration costs)
Net revenue$16.3 billion (+3% QoQ)
Non-interest expense$8.9 billion (-2% QoQ)
Pre-provision earnings$7.5 billion (+10% QoQ)
Net interest margin (NIM)8.41% (+0.40 pp QoQ)
Domestic card net charge-off rate3.98% (-0.65 pp YoY)
Common equity Tier 1 ratio (CET1)13.8%

Net income in the same quarter a year earlier was $3.2 billion ($4.83 per share). Net interest margin is the difference between the interest earned on loans and the interest paid on deposits and other funding, expressed as a percentage of loan assets, and is a key measure of a bank's profitability. Because credit cards make up a large share of its business, Capital One's figure runs far higher than that of a typical bank.

Interesting Point 1: Synergies Are Ahead of Schedule

Management said that about $1.8 billion of merger synergies, on an annualized basis, have been reflected in results this year, and that progress is ahead of schedule. The move of debit card payment processing to the Discover network is complete, and all new Discover card issuance is now handled on Capital One's technology platform. The credit card migration will not happen all at once; the company plans to proceed gradually, testing products and customers along the way.

Interesting Point 2: It's Not All Good News

  • Reserve release effect: This quarter, a $225 million release of loan-loss reserves helped earnings. The delinquency rate was 3.74%, and management explained that the recent trend is not an improvement beyond normal seasonal patterns.
  • Auto loans: The auto loan net charge-off rate rose to 1.59%. Management attributed this to a gradual increase in the share of subprime borrowers (those with lower credit scores).
  • Higher marketing spend: Quarterly marketing expense was about $1.6 billion, up 14% year over year, and is expected to rise further in Q4 and in 2027.
  • Declining Discover card loans: Discover card loan balances are expected to keep shrinking for several more quarters before returning to growth.
  • Payments fee uncertainty: If the Visa/Mastercard settlement is finalized, merchant fee (interchange) revenue could decline. Management expects the remaining synergies and this impact to roughly offset each other, but said the size of the settlement itself is highly uncertain.

The Brex Acquisition: Expanding into Corporate Cards

Capital One is also moving forward with its acquisition of Brex, a corporate spend management platform. For now, integration priority is on meeting regulatory and risk management requirements, and over the long term the company plans to connect Brex's spend management tools with Capital One's card, travel, and banking products. The 9% year-over-year increase in domestic card segment expenses also reflects the Brex impact, along with technology investment and marketing.

Shareholder Returns and Ownership

In Q3 the company repurchased $2.6 billion of its own shares, and the CET1 ratio held at 13.8%, similar to the prior quarter. CET1 is a measure of the strength of a bank's core capital, which absorbs losses in a crisis. Major shareholders are large index fund managers such as Vanguard, BlackRock, and State Street; it is not a holding of Korea's National Pension Service.

What Investors Should Watch

  • Whether credit costs stay stable even without reserve releases
  • How much the expansion of subprime auto lending pushes up charge-off rates
  • Whether cost-saving synergies offset rising marketing and technology investment
  • When the decline in Discover card loans reverses
  • The final terms of the Visa/Mastercard settlement

In sum, Q3 was a good quarter in which merger synergies and credit improvement appeared together, but it mixes in one-off-type reserve releases and rising cost factors, so the quality of earnings deserves scrutiny. That said, the above summarizes publicly disclosed results and management comments, and any outlook is only an estimate.
